edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource, transcribed from volume 1 of the Complete Works of Lu Xun (1948 printing); first published in The Short Story Magazine (小說月報) 13:12, December 1922, and collected in Call to Arms (吶喊), 1923.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，录自《鲁迅全集》第一卷（1948 年印本）；初刊于 1922 年 12 月《小说月报》第十三卷第十二号，收入《呐喊》（1923）。

basis.en: First published in 1922; the author died in 1936. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1922 年首次发表，作者卒于 1936 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: First two dismal evenings at the opera in Beijing, then the real subject: a boy's summer night on the river, a borrowed boat, a performance the children leave halfway through, and beans stolen and boiled on the way home. It is here because it shows how a remembered night becomes better than any later version of the same thing. Notice the last line, where the beans and the play are joined and neither can be had again.
note.zh: 先写在北京看戏的两回狼狈，然后才是真正要写的：一个孩子的夏夜，借来的航船，看到一半就走的戏，还有归途中偷来煮吃的罗汉豆。收在这里，是因为它写出了一个被记住的夜晚，如何胜过后来同样的东西。留意最后一句，豆和戏连在一起，都再也得不到了。

excerpt.orig: 眞的，一直到現在，我實在再沒有喫到那夜似的好豆，——也不再看到那夜似的好戲了。
excerpt.en: It is true. Right up to now, I have really never again eaten beans as good as those of that night, nor seen another opera as good as the one I saw that night.
excerpt.zh: 真的，一直到现在，我实在再没有吃到那夜似的好豆，——也不再看到那夜似的好戏了。
